title: mime-tree: no Content-Type defaults to octet-stream instead of RFC 2045 §5.2 text/plain
description: parse.rs build_part() falls back to 'application/octet-stream' when no Content-Type header is present. RFC 2045 §5.2 mandates the default is 'text/plain; charset=us-ascii'. Trigger: parse a MIME body part with no Content-Type header (e.g. a bare-text message body). Bad behavior: the part gets content_type='application/octet-stream', which is not text/plain, so RFC 8621 §4.1.4 is_inline check fails — the part goes to attachments instead of text_body/html_body. Users with legacy MUAs that omit Content-Type will see their message body classified as an attachment.
